title: Chicago Deep Dish Pizza
subtitle: thick crust pizza with chunky tomato topping
excerpt: A deep-dish pizza with a buttery crust, layered with cheese, meat, and a thick tomato sauce on top. It is more like a savoury pie than a traditional pizza. Allow time for the dough and the long bake.
sourceNotes: Chicago deep dish pizza was developed in the 1940s at Pizzeria Uno. The thick, pan-baked style with inverted layers became a Chicago institution and a point of local pride.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Make the dough the night before. Leave it to rise slowly in the fridge.

content.text: The layers go in an unusual order for deep dish -- cheese first, then meat, then tomato sauce on top. This stops the crust going soggy. Use a deep cast-iron skillet or a 30cm cake tin.

items.prepNote: Italian pork sausage, squeezed from casings

content.text: Mix the yeast with 180ml warm water. Leave for 5 minutes until frothy. Mix into the flour, butter, and salt to form a soft dough.
Knead for 5 minutes until smooth. Cover and leave in a warm place for 1 hour until doubled.
Brown the beef mince and sausage meat together in a frying pan. Drain excess fat. Season.
Make the sauce: cook the garlic in a little oil for 1 minute. Add the tomatoes and oregano. Simmer for 10 minutes.
Preheat oven to 200C (fan 180C / gas 6). Butter a deep 30cm cast-iron skillet or cake tin well.
Press the risen dough into the tin and up the sides to a height of about 4cm.
Layer the mozzarella slices over the base. Add the meat mixture. Spoon the tomato sauce on top. Scatter with parmesan.
Bake for 35 to 40 minutes until the crust is golden and the filling is bubbling. Rest for 10 minutes before cutting.

items.symptom: Dough is soggy at the base
items.cause: Filling too wet or oven not hot enough
items.fix: Drain the meat well after cooking. Make sure the tomato sauce is reduced and thick before it goes on top.

items.cause: Dough pressed too thickly or over-proofed
items.fix: Aim for about 1cm thickness on the base. Keep the sides a little thicker to hold the filling.

items.cause: Too much filling or sides not high enough
items.fix: Build the crust sides up to at least 4cm. Do not overfill.

content.text: Chicago deep dish pizza was developed at Pizzeria Uno in 1943. The founders wanted something hearty and different from the thin-crust New York style. The inverted layering, with cheese under the sauce, is what sets it apart. It is a point of fierce civic pride in Chicago and a source of equally fierce debate with New York pizza fans.
